source: TAT-2 expansion content built from the shipped Skybox distant-building kit
notes: KF11's mission-preparation frame stands the thief on a slate ridge with the Kilcairn skyline behind him. The two loaded lobby sublevels (MissionLobby_Geo3 + MissionLobby_Periphery) carry 2,107 meshes, 387 of which sit inside the authored CameraActor_0 10 deg half-angle; this file adds only the far-city layer the authored camera's sky sector does not already fill.

This file is original TAT-2 layout data, not extracted content: it places shipped Skybox meshes/materials (/Game/Art/Environment/Skybox/...) in a camera-relative ring. The runtime never rewrites the authored sublevels.

Placement contract (T05): azimuth_deg is measured from the prep camera's horizontal forward (+ = left, matching Godot's +Y rotation); distance_m is the horizontal metres; base_y is the ABSOLUTE world Y of the mesh AABB bottom (not camera-relative); yaw_deg is the node's Y rotation; scale is uniform.

Composition band (T05): under the authored camera (pitch +6.685 deg) the world horizon projects to screen y 1.09, so ground-level distant blocks appear as a low far-city layer. Each piece must satisfy, on its projected mesh AABB: width <= 0.60 frame widths, top edge in screen y [0.65, 0.98], and horizontal overlap with the 0..1 frame. game/tests/test_t05_ui_contract.gd enforces this against the real spawned meshes.

The previous authoring (scales 1.0-1.7 at the same standoffs) produced a near block 1.55 frame widths wide whose top cut through the mid-frame: 2-5x the stated distant-city contract. The pre-T05 standoff note ('DistantBuildingC is 24.4 m tall at scale 1, so the roofline band needs ~300-500 m standoff and a >1 scale') was fitted to a reframed camera and is retired.
layer is documentation only: near = KF11 foreground mass, mid = the roofline band, far = the horizon row behind it.
